newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea Nelson output down, more cuts seen-source.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea Nelson output down, more cuts seen-source.

text.p: Production at the North Sea Nelson oilfield could fall briefly below 50,000 barrels per day (bpd) next week from the current level of 110,000 bpd to allow repairs to gas dehydration equipment, a source at operator Enterprise Oil said on Friday.
"It will have to come down significantly around the middle to end of next week," the source said.
"We may even have to take a total outage for a day or two -- certainly below 50,000 (bpd)," he said.
The source said production had been lowered to around 110,000 bpd from 130,000 earlier on Friday and the further cuts would be made from the middle of next week to prevent excess gas flaring.
Output was lowered earlier this week to between 120,000 and 130,000 from the normal output level of around 140,000 bpd as a reuslt of the fault.

The problem at Nelson, which feeds the Forties system, has so far resulted in the deferral to the August loading programe of about 1.25 million barrels of Forties originally scheduled to load in July.
The fault has occurred in glycol dehydration equipment that dries associated gas used in secondary recovery of the crude.
Enterprise said that as a result of the fault all gas produced at the Nelson field was currently being flared.

The field had to lower output to about 53,000 bpd in June to allow repairs to a faulty gas compressor. Production was restored gradually to around 140,000 bpd late in June after the repair was completed.
